checks.message: The second byte is not the inverse of the address. This may be extended NEC with a 16-bit address.
The fourth byte is not the inverse of the command: a bit was misread.

info.what: Output of an IR receiver module. Rests high, goes low while the remote sends.
info.confirm: Starts with 9 ms low and 4.5 ms high. Then 32 bits: each has a 560 µs low mark; a short gap after it is 0 and a long gap is 1.
info.decoderTips: One channel. The 32 bits are address, inverted address, command, inverted command.
info.lookalikes: Other remote formats (RC5, Sony) use different start pulses.

symptoms.symptom: Only a short burst repeats while a button is held
symptoms.cause: NEC repeat codes: 9 ms low, 2.25 ms high, one mark
symptoms.action: Normal. The command is in the first, long frame.

symptoms.cause: Extended NEC with a 16-bit address, or a misread bit
symptoms.action: If only the address pair fails, it is extended NEC.
